scenes.headline: How a harness learns to solve longer, unseen tasks
scenes.sub: Recursive Language Models keep every call in distribution
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Crumpet! Transformers struggle to recombine what they know on bigger problems. Zhang and Khattab argue the fix can live in the harness, not the weights.

scenes.text: Keep every model call locally in-distribution: split a huge task so each call sees only a short, familiar slice.
scenes.say: The idea: keep every model call locally in distribution. Split a huge task so each call only sees a short, familiar slice.

scenes.title: Two ways to read a long task

left.title: Base Transformer
items: Reads the whole task in one window
Past its training length, the context rots
left.say: A base Transformer reads the whole task in one window. Past the lengths it trained on, that context is unfamiliar, and it degrades.

right.title: Recursive Language Model
items: Each call sees a short, familiar slice
Accuracy holds as the task grows
right.say: A Recursive Language Model decomposes it, so every call sees something short and familiar, and accuracy holds as the task grows.

scenes.title: How the RLM keeps its window small

steps.say: First, context offloading. The long input isn't pasted into the prompt. It's stored as a variable in a REPL.
The root model sees a short prefix and a symbolic handle, and peeks at the data through small probes.
Second, programmatic sub-calls. Sub-agents run like functions, and their outputs land in variables, not back in the root's context.

steps.note: the root's context stays short, however long the task
steps.say: So the root's window stays small and familiar, however long the task grows.

items.text: RL-train the harness on short tasks
items.say: They train the harness with reinforcement learning on short tasks: a hundred and fifty steps, on a thirty-billion-parameter Qwen model.
On held-out tasks eight to thirty-two times longer, its reward tracks training. The base Transformer's stays flat.
It even transfers across domains, from sorting Jeopardy questions to spotting spam. What transfers is the decomposition strategy.

scenes.text: Where an inductive bias lives is a design choice. Here, the layer around the model is the part that generalizes.

recap: Offload the context into REPL variables
scenes.say: To recap: offload the context, call sub-agents like functions, and train short to generalize long.
